_comment: COUPLING tier-2. The COMPARATIVE half of the accelerator advice, and the MEASURED BOUNDARY that goes with it: 'over the whole grid Aitken matched or beat the same constant theta in 65 of the 70 settings' and 'at rho = 6 and rho = 9 it solved NOTHING and landed on NOTHING. At every theta on the grid it diverged, by 4.1e+03 to 2.0e+17 relative'. One strongly unbalanced ratio and the one theta the knowledge hands an agent who cannot estimate rho ('first try, cannot estimate rho at all: theta=0.5, keep accelerator=aitken'), racing the two accelerators under an IDENTICAL max_iter and tol read back from each run rather than assumed. ||| WHAT CHANGED AND WHY. This fixture used to require the DEFAULT to REACH the closed form at rho = 6, on the strength of a preamble asserting rho = 6 was 'inside the region the default still recovers'. It was red for months. The preamble was never measured on this driver: it came from a 40-cell sweep run on the PER-PARTICIPANT Aitken theta that feature/coupling-robustness replaced with one global theta, on an analytic stand-in for the participants, with a harness that was never committed. Re-measured over 70 settings with scripts/sweep_accelerators.py on the driver and participants that ship: at theta = 0.5 the default SOLVES up to rho = 2 and no further; at rho = 4 it lands on the answer (1.2e-05 relative) without its residual reaching tol in 300 iterations; at rho = 6 and 9 it solves nothing and lands on nothing at ANY theta. So rho = 6 is outside the recovery region by two swept ratios and the fixture was demanding more than the knowledge claims. The ASSERTION is corrected to what the claim says — matched or beat — and the ratio is NOT moved to one where the default wins, because moving it would be choosing the setting that makes a sentence true instead of measuring it. rho = 6 is kept precisely because it is where the two halves come apart: the default loses the absolute contest and wins the comparative one by about thirty orders of magnitude, so the fixture also pins the boundary and fails if either half moves. ||| WHAT IS NOT PINNED: the gap is asserted as a FLOOR of 10 orders, never as a value. The constant arm is bit-reproducible here; the Aitken arm is not reproducible across environments, because its theta is a nonlinear clamped function of the residual history and on a diverging run a last-bit difference in a BLAS reduction changes which adaptation hits the clamp. The verdict was identical in every environment tried; the digits were not.

_mutation.note: Move the ratio to a balanced one, where theta=0.5 IS 1/(1+rho) and therefore already the optimum. The imbalance the claim is about disappears and the fixture fails four ways: the premise assertion fires because 0.5 is now below the stability limit 2/(1+rho)=1.0, the constant arm reaches the closed form so constant_reached_closed_form prints True, the Aitken arm reaches it too so the boundary assertion fires, and aitken_also_diverged prints False. This is the mutation that matters for a COMPARATIVE claim measured at a specific ratio — it breaks neither accelerator, it removes the imbalance, and only a fixture that picked a ratio where the naive theta is genuinely bad notices.
